title: Joomukbap is a Korean style rice ball
summary: Literal translation is “fist rice”, because the rice ball is the size of a fist! This meal is easy to make, yet super nutritious.
ingredients: 1 cup of cooked ground meat + seasoning (I used ground beef, and added 1 tablespoon of soy sauce), for younger babies, skip seasoning.
1 cup of cooked, chopped vegetables (I recommend carrots, broccoli and mushroom — less moisture, easier to shape)
steps: Mix cooked rice, cooked meat, and vegetables in a bowl * Add and mix in 1 tablespoon of Sesame oil * Shape the mixture into balls!
Optional: shred roasted seaweed in a bowl, roll the rice ball and cover it with the seaweed Feel free to season as desired for older toddlers, kids & adults.
Adding 1-3 tablespoons of soy sauce will enhance flavor.
caption: Joomukbap is a Korean style rice ball — literal translation is “fist rice”, because the rice ball is the size of a fist! This meal is easy to make, yet super nutritious. You have your vegetables, meat, grains and fat/oil. Below is the recipe! I prefer 1 to 1 ratio of cooked rice to all other ingredients (veggies + meat). Below is what I used:   * 2 cups of cooked rice (Short-grain rice or sushi rice works best, because they are sticky. Jasmine rice or long rice are less sticky and will not work) * 1 cup of cooked ground meat + seasoning (I used ground beef, and added 1 tablespoon of soy sauce), for younger babies, skip seasoning.  * 1 cup of cooked, chopped vegetables (I recommend carrots, broccoli and mushroom — less moisture, easier to shape) * Mix cooked rice, cooked meat, and vegetables in a bowl * Add and mix in 1 tablespoon of Sesame oil * Shape the mixture into balls! * Optional: shred roasted seaweed in a bowl, roll the rice ball and cover it with the seaweed  Feel free to season as desired for older toddlers, kids & adults.
